facts.value: Schaeffer et al. 2023: emergent abilities are largely a metric artifact — with smooth token-level metrics (target logprob, acceptability) improvement is continuous from early training; discontinuous metrics (exact match, pass@1) manufacture the phase transition. Practical transfer: score the log-probability of the correct answer against matched wrong ones instead of exact-matching generation

config.scope: metric granularity vs apparent emergence; token-level smooth metrics show continuous improvement

facts.value: CLiMP (Xiang et al. 2021) is the Chinese minimal-pair prior art: 16 syntactic contrasts across 9 Mandarin phenomena, 1000 pairs/contrast, 95.8% human agreement, template-generated over an annotated vocab (3456 words, 84 features), matched sentence length per pair, one paradigm discarded for <85% human agreement. Best: classifier-noun agreement, verb complement selection; worst: ba construction, binding, filler-gap. Chinese BERT 81.8%, LSTMs moderately above chance. github.com/beileixiang/CLiMP. Newer: ZhoBLiMP (arXiv 2411.06096), MultiBLiMP (arXiv 2504.02768)
facts.source: Xiang et al. 2021, arXiv 2101.11131 (full text extracted); docs/lessons/base_eval_at_200m.md §2

facts.value: construction rules for zh minimal pairs: (1) one controlled edit, matched character length AND matched tokenization — BPE merges across the edit boundary break the comparison (22% of our first draft failed: 他在 merges while 他再 does not, 吃了 merges in SVO but not SOV, 这本书 is one token); assert equal token length, contiguous diff span for substitutions, identical token multiset for permutations; skip and report failures. (2) score = full-sentence sum logprob, length-matched so no normalization. (3) known-answer: swap labels, must invert, >=60pt spread on the strongest checkpoint. (4) human spot-check per dimension (CLiMP discarded a paradigm below 85% agreement)
facts.source: docs/lessons/base_eval_at_200m.md §2; eval/base_matrix.py align_pairs() (277/303 pairs aligned after the merge fixes)

facts.value: at a 50% floor, SE=sqrt(0.25/n): n=100 -> 5.0%, n=277 -> 3.0%, n=1000 (BLiMP/CLiMP) -> 1.6%, n=4900 -> 0.7%. Minimum detectable delta at 80% power: ~14pt at n=100, ~8.4pt at n=277, ~4.4pt at n=1000, 2pt at n=4900. Resolving 2 points needs ~4900 pairs/dimension; 1000/dimension is the proven operating point for tracking a 16x ladder
facts.source: computed: n=((z_a+z_b)*0.5/delta)^2, z_a=1.96 two-sided, z_b=0.84; docs/lessons/base_eval_at_200m.md §2

config.resolution_formula: MDE=2.8*sqrt(p(1-p)/n); p=0.5 worst case -> 1.4/sqrt(n); two-sided alpha=0.05, power=0.8

facts.value: the MC floor is mostly a suite problem: ceval (Chinese) moves while 4 English benchmarks don't on the SAME model and scale — benchmark language is isolated as the cause. A zh-pretrained model on English MC measures English exposure (~0 by corpus design), confounded twice: size (MC near chance below ~400M even in-language) and language (English fragments under a zh-optimized 32K vocab). Supporting: Pythia's BLOOM analysis — multilinguality penalty is benchmark-dependent. Recommendation: drop English MC from the base matrix, keep ceval as a z-value tripwire
facts.source: docs/lessons/base_eval_at_200m.md §4; Biderman et al. 2023 (BLOOM curse-of-multilinguality analysis)

facts.value: synthesized ordering of when metrics leave the floor: domain loss -> token-level target logprob / acceptability minimal pairs -> LAMBADA-style constrained prediction -> MC commonsense (~410M+) -> few-shot ICL -> generation. The 'loss moves but capability does not' gap is mostly metric granularity (Schaeffer), not a model waiting period. Likelihood measures recognition not production — necessary, not sufficient
